subject: Biotechnology
title: Memory Circuits
description: A short lesson to help you apply Memory Circuits.

hook.text: Cells that remember — genetic memory circuits record environmental events permanently in DNA.

buildup.text: Recombinases flip DNA segments — once flipped, the change is inherited by all future generations of cells.

discovery.text: SCRIBE uses CRISPR to write analog signals into DNA — the mutation rate encodes the intensity of a stimulus.

twist.text: Living cells as data storage — one gram of DNA can theoretically hold 215 petabytes of information.

climax.text: Gut bacteria engineered with memory circuits record inflammation events — diagnostic sensors that travel with you.

punchline.text: Write history into DNA — memory circuits make cells that never forget.

quiz.question: How do recombinase-based memory circuits store information?
options: They produce proteins that accumulate over time as a record
They flip DNA segments permanently, creating an inheritable record of an event
They store information in RNA that persists for several cell divisions
